Two independent fair binary covariates, deterministic Y0=(-1,4), Y1=(0,1), and independent treatment randomization from each feasible policy. Omega=Bool with the fair Bernoulli law; T is constantly false, R is the Boolean sample, Y0=0 and Y1=1. All variables are measurable and integrable; potential outcomes are constant and independent of T. A has mass 1, A1 and A0 each have mass 1/2, so q=1/2 and every branch can apply. Probability, independence and denominator positivity are checked in scratch/Check.lean.

Take n=1, alpha=1, beta=1/4 and eta=0. Fair private types, deterministic potential outcomes and estimator zero give Gamma=1 and regret 7/8 at reward-best (1,0). With beta=eta=1/4 the unique reward-best policy is (1,0), with regret 3/4. For arbitrary positive alpha,epsilon, choosing beta=min(epsilon,alpha/2), and delta equal to that minimum in the unique-response variant, supplies the required positive parameters and lower bounds. All laws are finite probability laws.

A counterexample satisfies every premise: n=1, fair binary X, deterministic Y0=0 and Y1(false)=1,Y1(true)=2, zero estimator, and P_pi(X=x,T=t)=(1/2)*coinMass(pi(x),t). Conditional ignorability is automatic for deterministic potential outcomes given X, all fixed-query estimator means are zero, and all quantities are integrable on the finite space. The printed rule (0,1) earns 1, while (1,1) earns 3/2 for both ATO and ATT. The one-unit score identity and these reward values are checked in scratch/Check.lean.

A counterexample uses n=1, fair binary X, Y0=0,Y1=1, P_pi(X=x,T=t)=(1/2)*coinMass(pi(x),t), and the same estimator procedure for every policy: hat_mu(sample,query)=2 when query=X(sample), otherwise -2. At each fixed query its mean is zero; at the evaluated query X it is constantly 2. Thus Standing and pointwise unbiasedness hold on the finite probability space. Expected TT is -(a+b)/2, best at (0,0); welfare is (a+b)/2, best at (1,1), so the reward-best policy has regret 1. Fixed-query means, the reward formula and its maximizing policy are checked in scratch/Check.lean.
